html:
SMTO-SKL-0028 — The calendar task stopped before it finished

GUID: ec3e551d-915d-5b0c-86a6-af669151f64d
Slug: google-calendar-operation-cancelled
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The task was stopped, so SMTO didn't send its next request to Google. Anything finished before it stopped, such as an event already created, stays in your calendar.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Calendar and check which of the changes you asked for are already there. Earlier steps may have finished before the task stopped, and stopping doesn't undo them.
  2. If you still want the rest done, ask SMTO again and tell it what's already finished. This avoids repeating changes that already happened, such as creating an event twice.

What success looks like

  • Google Calendar shows each change you wanted exactly once.

If it still fails

  • If you didn't stop the task yourself with Stop current task, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat the whole original request before checking your calendar; parts of it may already be done.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Calendar client saw its cancellation event set at a checkpoint before sending its next Google request; work completed by earlier steps or requests is not undone.

What this means

  • Calendar request cancellation is set at a cancellation checkpoint before further provider work. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Calendar request cancellation is set at a cancellation checkpoint before further provider work.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained prior receipts and the last completed request.

How to fix it

  • The operation stopped before the next provider request. Inspect earlier step results in the Run for completed Calendar changes, then explicitly request only the remaining work.
  • The operation stopped before the next provider request. Inspect any earlier receipts before explicitly requesting more work.

Retry and execution caution

  • The operation stopped before the next provider request. Inspect any earlier receipts before explicitly requesting more work.

How to verify the fix

  • Further work is explicitly resumed only after earlier effects are understood.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
